claims.text: USGS recorded a magnitude 7.4 earthquake on 10 August 2026 at 12:34:28 UTC, located 5 km S of San José del Palmar, Colombia (4.8436°N, -76.2422°W) at a depth of 110.3 km. USGS's PAGER system assessed an Orange alert level, with approximately 10.5 million people exposed to Strong-to-Very-Strong (MMI VI+) shaking.

Re-checked 12 August 2026: GDACS's earthquake report for this event (event id 1557236, episode 1724218) has escalated to an Overall Red alert for high humanitarian impact, with a GDACS score of 2.2 (up from 1.7) and about 5.2 million people now within zones of MMI VII or greater shaking (up from about 1.5 million). The page's casualty line, citing media reports and not independently verified by GDACS, now reads 'at least 240 deaths' -- higher than, and not adopted in place of, the government-sourced UN News figure below.

UN News (11 August 2026), 'Colombia earthquake: UN joins national response': citing Colombia's president, 'more than 180 have died' and 'hundreds have been injured'; 'nearly 5,000 homes have been damaged and 387 have been destroyed'; '61 buildings have collapsed'; 'more than 550 educational institutions, 24 health facilities and more than 350 community centres have [been] affected'; the government has activated emergency coordination centres in Bogotá, Quibdó, Armenia and Cali and has requested UN support.

Servicio Geológico Colombiano (10 August 2026): confirms the magnitude 7.4 event centered near San José del Palmar at a depth of about 103 km, recorded 18 aftershocks (magnitude 1.4-4.8) as of midday 10 August, describes it as 'the seismic event of greatest magnitude recorded in Colombia in the 21st century,' and notes more than 12,000 people from 900 populated centres reported feeling the earthquake. The bulletin gives no casualty figures.

USGS's PAGER alert for the earthquake (event us6000tjl2) escalated to Red as of 13 August 2026 06:30:47 UTC (magnitude 7.4, MMI 7.999, CDI 7.9, 1,121 felt reports), up from the Orange level recorded 11 August 2026.

OCHA Colombia's Flash Update 004 (posted 13 August 2026, data as of 12 August 18:30 local time): 'The emergency continues to escalate and has exceeded the local response capacity, with at least 49,214 people affected, 30,324 families impacted, 3,771 injured people, and 241 fatalities across 13 departments of the country... Damage to more than 54,900 homes (destroyed and damaged)... the USD 5 million CERF allocation represents a critical boost to scale up the emergency response.'

OCHA Colombia, Flash Update 005 (as of 13 August, 18:30 local time): "The scale of the emergency continues to grow. Heavy rainfall and related impacts have affected 53,816 people (25,872 families) across at least 13 departments and 401 municipalities nationwide, including 266 deaths and 11,789 homes destroyed. The most affected departments are Risaralda, Valle del Cauca, Chocó and Caldas. However, the emergency continues to expand and figures may increase due to access constraints and possible underreporting."

OCHA Colombia's Flash Update No. 006 (data as of 14 August 2026, 18:30 local time): 287 deaths, 3,975 injured, 378 missing, 135,179 affected people (56,448 affected families) across 15 departments and 437 municipalities, 13,077 homes destroyed; 183 aftershocks have followed the mainshock (15 of magnitude >3, two >4); an initial US$5 million CERF allocation is supporting the response.

description: A magnitude 7.4 intermediate-depth earthquake struck western Colombia on 10 August 2026 at 12:34:28 UTC, centered 5 km S of San José del Palmar in Chocó Department, about 240 km west of Bogotá, at a depth of roughly 110 km. USGS's PAGER system assessed an Orange alert level, with an estimated 10.5 million people exposed to strong-to-very-strong shaking (MMI VI+). GDACS initially assessed the event as an Orange alert for medium humanitarian impact; re-checked 12 August 2026, GDACS has escalated the event to a Red alert for high humanitarian impact, with its score rising from 1.7 to 2.2 and its population-exposure estimate for MMI VII+ shaking rising from about 1.5 million to about 5.2 million. UN News (11 August 2026) reports that Colombia's government has confirmed 'more than 180' deaths, hundreds injured, nearly 5,000 homes damaged (387 destroyed), 61 buildings collapsed, and more than 550 educational institutions, 24 health facilities and 350 community centres affected; the government has activated emergency coordination centres in Bogotá, Quibdó, Armenia and Cali and requested UN support. Colombia's national geological survey (SGC) recorded 18 aftershocks (M1.4-4.8) as of midday 10 August and described the mainshock as the strongest recorded in Colombia in the 21st century. Bogotá's own emergency-management office (IDIGER) inspected nearly 4,800 homes/offices in the capital and found no moderate or severe structural damage there, indicating the worst damage is concentrated in Chocó, Valle del Cauca, Caldas and Risaralda rather than the capital. Colombian news media have reported that President Abelardo De la Espriella signed a national-disaster decree; this decree itself remains unconfirmed by a directly-fetched allowlisted source, though UN News does confirm the government has activated emergency coordination centres. OCHA Colombia's Flash Update 004 (12 August 2026) reports the emergency 'continues to escalate and has exceeded the local response capacity,' with the confirmed toll rising to 241 deaths, 3,771 injured, 49,214 people affected and 30,324 families impacted across 13 departments, and damage to more than 54,900 homes; USGS's PAGER alert was raised from Orange to Red the same day (magnitude 7.4, 1,121 felt reports). Re-checked 14 August 2026: OCHA Colombia's Flash Update 005 (posted 14 August 2026, data as of 13 August 18:30 local time) reports 266 deaths and 53,816 people (25,872 families) affected across 13 departments and 401 municipalities, with 11,789 homes destroyed — up from 241 deaths and 49,214 people affected in Flash Update 004. USGS and GDACS alert levels remain Red, unchanged. Re-checked 15 August 2026: OCHA Colombia's Flash Update 006 (posted 15 August 2026, data as of 14 August 18:30 local time) reports the affected population has risen sharply to at least 135,179 people across 15 departments (up from 13) and 437 municipalities (up from 401), with 183 aftershocks recorded five days after the mainshock and an initial US$5 million CERF allocation supporting the international response; the report gives no updated death toll or homes-destroyed figure in its accessible summary text. GDACS's report page (still Red alert) carries a media-echo citation from Italian outlet ITALPRESS of "at least 281 deaths and 3,900 injured," attributed to third-party media rather than to GDACS's own assessment, USGS, or OCHA; this figure is not adopted and the confirmed toll remains 266 deaths per OCHA Flash Update 005 (13 August). USGS and GDACS alert levels remain Red, unchanged. Re-checked 16 August 2026: OCHA Colombia's Flash Update 006 (data as of 14 August 18:30 local time) raises the confirmed toll to 287 deaths, 3,975 injured and 378 missing, with 135,179 people (56,448 families) affected across 15 departments and 437 municipalities and 13,077 homes destroyed; 183 aftershocks have now been recorded and an initial US$5 million CERF allocation is supporting the international response. Re-checked 17 August 2026: no OCHA Colombia Flash Update newer than No. 006 (14 August data) was found via search, and direct fetch of ReliefWeb's Colombia earthquake disaster page (reliefweb.int/disaster/eq-2026-000146-col) returned HTTP 403; GDACS's event report (episode 1724218) remains at Red alert with the same media-echo casualty citation ("at least 281 deaths and 3,900 injured," attributed to Italian outlet ITALPRESS, not independently verified by GDACS) already on file, and USGS's PAGER event page remains inaccessible via direct fetch (browser-only interface, as since 11 August). The confirmed toll remains 287 deaths per OCHA Flash Update 006 (14 August data).
